page3_img_1.png.title: Interview participant breakdown by role, seniority, and count
page3_img_1.png.description: A three-column table showing the disciplines interviewed, their level of seniority, and the number of people interviewed in each cell. Software Engineers are the largest group: Entry Level 4, Senior 1, Principal and Above 4, Manager 5, Upper Management 11 (25 total). Product Managers appear as Principal and Above 3, Manager 3, Upper Management 11 (17 total); additional participants include Designer (Principal and Above: 2), Data Science (Principal and Above: 1), and Architect (Principal and Above: 3). The table entries sum to 48 interviewees, while the paper text reports 47 interviews, indicating a one-person discrepancy.

page7_img_1.png.title: Top challenges in adopting OKRs (percentage of mentions)
page7_img_1.png.description: Horizontal bar chart showing the frequency with which survey respondents mentioned particular challenges when working with OKRs. The most-cited problem is “Creating OKRs/Goals” (about 35–40% of responses), followed by “Data Issues” (roughly 20–25%). Other commonly reported challenges include “Working With Others,” “Priorities,” and “Alignment, Accountability, Clarity & Transparency” (each ≈15–18%), with “Lack of Process,” “Overall Frustration,” “Goals Across Levels,” and “Goal Review & Communication” mentioned less often (roughly 8–15% each). The figure visualizes open-text themes from the survey, and totals exceed 100% because respondents could report multiple challenges.
